instruction: Rigid Body Bake to Keyframes `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains: - A `Ground` box (20x20x0.2 BU, top face at z=0) set as a PASSIVE rigid body with MESH collision shape. - 10 cubes named `Cube_00`, `Cube_01`, ..., `Cube_09` (size 1 BU each), stacked vertically above the ground at Z = 0.5, 2.0, 3.5, 5.0, 6.5, 8.0, 9.5, 11.0, 12.5, 14.0 (center-to-center spacing of 1.5 BU, leaving a 0.5 BU air gap between each pair). Each cube is ACTIVE rigid body with MESH collision, mass = 1.0. - A rigid body world exists with `point_cache.frame_end = 120`. Scene frame range is 1..120. Gravity is (0, 0, -9.81). - The simulation has NOT been baked. Your task: 1. Run the rigid body simulation for frames 1..120 so the stack of cubes falls under gravity and collides, settling on the ground. 2. Bake the simulated transforms (location + rotation) to keyframes on every cube for frames 1..120. Every cube must end up with at least 120 keyframes on its location f-curves and at least 120 keyframes on its rotation f-curves. 3. Remove the rigid body world entirely so the motion is driven purely by the keyframes: select every cube and the ground, call `bpy.ops.rigidbody.objects_remove()` to strip the rigid body settings, then call `bpy.ops.rigidbody.world_remove()`. After this, `bpy.context.scene.rigidbody_world` must be `None`. 4. Save the scene to `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. Requirements =============== 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists and opens. 2. Mesh objects `Cube_00`..`Cube_09` are present. 3. `scene.rigidbody_world` is `None`. 4. Every cube has location f-curves with at least 120 keyframe points each. 5. Every cube has rotation (euler or quaternion) f-curves with at least 120 keyframe points each. 6. At frame 120, no cube's world Z falls below -0.01 (all cubes rest on/above the ground). 7. The stack has collapsed: at least 5 of the 10 cubes have moved >= 0.1 BU (Euclidean distance) from their frame-1 position to their frame-120 position. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal.
